_meta.purpose: Grounded symptom->fix knowledge dictated by Teddy (owner/master tech). Feeds the Ant customer chat, tech diagnostic assist, and brand/symptom web pages. Every entry is a real, common repair TN Appliance does. 'easy' = fast, affordable, high-margin. 'smarthq' = on newer GE we read it via SmartHQ factory diagnostics.
_meta.rules: Never quote a part number to a customer. Warranty jobs never hit a payment screen. Use this to lead with the exact symptom the customer describes, then the honest fix.

entries.likely_cause: linear compressor failure
entries.fix: Check the LG 10-year limited compressor-part warranty first; if covered the customer mostly pays labor. Replace compressor.
entries.note: The famous LG failure. Warranty check is the money-saver and the trust-builder.

entries.likely_cause: ice maker assembly, water inlet valve, or frozen line
entries.fix: Replace ice maker assembly / inlet valve.

entries.likely_cause: drain pump clogged (coin/hairpin/lint) or worn
entries.fix: Clear or replace drain pump; check drain hose.

entries.likely_cause: worn suspension rods, bad shock, or balance sensor
French-door ice maker frost-up (airflow + seal)
entries.fix: Fix root cause (airflow/seal) and install improved-revision module so it stays fixed. Do NOT just swap the module.
entries.note: Our Samsung specialty. Most shops swap the module and it fails again.

entries.likely_cause: defrost system or frosted evaporator choking airflow
entries.fix: Defrost repair (heater/sensor/control). Not a dead compressor = affordable.

entries.likely_cause: evaporator fan hitting ice buildup behind back panel
entries.fix: Clear ice, fix root cause, replace fan if damaged.

entries.likely_cause: worn suspension rods or tired balance ring
entries.note: Whirlpools are almost always worth fixing.

entries.likely_cause: drain pump clogged or worn
main control board fault
defrost system or stuck air damper starving fresh-food airflow
entries.fix: Defrost/damper repair. Affordable, not a dead compressor.

entries.likely_cause: condenser fan, main control, or sealed system/compressor
water inlet valve, stuck float/float switch, or tripped flood-float
blown thermal fuse, failed door latch/switch, or main control
drain pump clogged or worn
suspension rods, shift actuator, or hall sensor
heating element (electric) / igniter (gas) / blown thermal fuse
entries.fix: Replace element/igniter/fuse; clear the vent so the fuse doesn't blow again.

entries.likely_cause: belt, idler pulley, or drum rollers
worn igniter or dirty/misaligned burner cap
bake element (electric) or oven igniter (gas), or temp sensor
n/a
entries.fix: On newer GE, connect via SmartHQ to read every stored error code and run factory diagnostic tests for an exact diagnosis before opening a panel.
entries.note: Our GE moat. Most independents can't do this.

symptoms: iced up on back of freezer
entries.likely_cause: clogged / frozen defrost drain tube (backs up, refreezes, overflows into fridge or onto floor)
entries.fix: Clear and thaw the defrost drain, install drain heater/clip so it doesn't re-clog.
entries.note: THE most common fridge repair, cross-brand. Especially Samsung; also Frigidaire and GE side-by-sides; and virtually all top-freezers (ice on the bottom or water leaking into the fridge).

entries.likely_cause: failed LED light board/module (common on newer LED-lit fridges)
entries.note: Many newer fridges use LED boards that fail as a unit.

entries.likely_cause: weak oven glow-bar igniter — draws current but doesn't get hot enough to open the safety valve quickly, so gas pools then lights with a boom (or the oven never heats)
entries.note: Easy money. All gas stoves. The delayed-ignition boom and gas smell are the tell.

entries.likely_cause: compressor start relay / overload failing to start the compressor (usually NOT a dead compressor)
entries.fix: Test and replace the start relay/overload — cheap, fast, often brings the fridge right back.
entries.note: We love older fridges and top-freezers. The click-every-few-minutes + warm is the tell; test the relay before condemning the compressor.

entries.likely_cause: motor coupler, lid switch, or drain pump on the well-documented direct-drive platform
entries.fix: Replace the cheap sacrificial part (coupler/lid switch/pump).
entries.note: Old washers make us happy — parts are cheap and available even on 15+ year units. Almost always worth fixing.

entries.likely_cause: worn drum rollers, tired idler pulley, worn drum glides, or a bad rear bearing
entries.fix: Replace the worn rollers/idler/glides/bearing — dryer runs quiet again.
entries.note: Squeaky dryers get desqueaked. Fast, cheap, high-margin.
